provenance: Synthetic cases authored during evaluation design. Labels are provisional, not an independently adjudicated benchmark.
scope: Assess the candidate claim for the stated reader task using only the supplied sources and variable bindings. Do not grade general prose preference.

families.capability: Preserve the prerequisite for an action
families.reader_task: An owner needs to know when workspace removal is available.

sources.text: In the standard workspace, Remove becomes available only after the export finishes. Before then, removal is unavailable.

variants.text: You can remove the workspace only after its export finishes.

expected.rationale: Preserves the governing claim for this reader task.

sources.text: In the standard workspace, Remove becomes available only after the export finishes. Before then, removal is unavailable.

variants.text: Wait for the export to finish before removing the workspace.

expected.rationale: Changes wording while preserving the governing claim.

sources.text: In the standard workspace, Remove becomes available only after the export finishes. Before then, removal is unavailable.

variants.text: You can remove the workspace before its export finishes.

expected.rationale: Permits removal before the required export has finished.

sources.text: In the temporary workspace, Remove is available both before and after an export finishes.

variants.text: You can remove the workspace before its export finishes.

expected.rationale: The identical candidate is supported under this different governing context.

families.reader_task: A reader chooses a workspace that supports the required sharing method.

sources.text: New standard workspaces allow public links. Archive workspaces never allow public links.

variants.text: You can create public links in new standard workspaces, but not in archive workspaces.

expected.rationale: Preserves the governing claim for this reader task.

sources.text: New standard workspaces allow public links. Archive workspaces never allow public links.

variants.text: Public links are available for new standard workspaces. Archive workspaces do not offer them.

expected.rationale: Changes wording while preserving the governing claim.

sources.text: New standard workspaces allow public links. Archive workspaces never allow public links.

variants.text: Public links are available in all workspaces, including archive workspaces.

expected.rationale: Extends public-link availability to archive workspaces despite the explicit exception.

sources.text: All workspaces, including archive workspaces, allow public links.

variants.text: Public links are available in all workspaces, including archive workspaces.

expected.rationale: The identical candidate is supported under this different governing context.

families.reader_task: An editor needs to know whether to send an invitation or ask an owner.

sources.text: Only workspace owners can invite guests. Editors can edit files but cannot invite guests.

variants.text: Guest invitations are available only to workspace owners.

expected.rationale: Preserves the governing claim for this reader task.

sources.text: Only workspace owners can invite guests. Editors can edit files but cannot invite guests.

variants.text: To invite a guest, you must be a workspace owner.

expected.rationale: Changes wording while preserving the governing claim.

sources.text: Only workspace owners can invite guests. Editors can edit files but cannot invite guests.

variants.text: Workspace owners and editors can invite guests.

expected.rationale: Grants guest-invitation permission to editors, whom the source explicitly excludes.

sources.text: Workspace owners and editors can both invite guests.

variants.text: Workspace owners and editors can invite guests.

expected.rationale: The identical candidate is supported under this different governing context.

sources.text: Workspace owners can invite guests. This extract does not specify editor permissions.

variants.text: Workspace editors can invite guests.

expected.rationale: The source neither grants nor denies editor invitations. Request the missing permission rule rather than inventing one.

families.capability: Preserve the strength of a claim
families.reader_task: A reader decides what to expect after retrying a failed upload.

sources.text: Retrying a failed upload may restore it. A retry is not guaranteed to succeed.

variants.text: Retrying may restore the failed upload, but success is not guaranteed.

expected.rationale: Preserves the governing claim for this reader task.

sources.text: Retrying a failed upload may restore it. A retry is not guaranteed to succeed.

variants.text: A retry can help recover the upload; it might still fail.

expected.rationale: Changes wording while preserving the governing claim.

sources.text: Retrying a failed upload may restore it. A retry is not guaranteed to succeed.

variants.text: Retrying will always restore the failed upload.

expected.rationale: Turns an explicitly uncertain recovery step into a guarantee.

sources.text: For this simulated upload exercise, every retry is guaranteed to restore the failed upload.

variants.text: Retrying will always restore the failed upload.

expected.rationale: The identical candidate is supported under this different governing context.

sources.text: Uploads can fail. This extract does not describe automatic recovery.

variants.text: A failed upload will be restored automatically.

expected.rationale: The source does not establish whether automatic recovery exists. The candidate is unsupported, but its opposite is not established either.

families.capability: Preserve the relationship between named participants
families.reader_task: A reader identifies who submits and who approves access requests for Cedar.

sources.text: For the Cedar workspace, Mira approves access requests submitted by Leon. Leon cannot approve requests from Mira.

variants.text: Mira approves access requests from Leon for the Cedar workspace.

expected.rationale: Preserves the governing claim for this reader task.

sources.text: For the Cedar workspace, Mira approves access requests submitted by Leon. Leon cannot approve requests from Mira.

variants.text: Access requests Leon submits for Cedar are approved by Mira.

expected.rationale: Changes wording while preserving the governing claim.

sources.text: For the Cedar workspace, Mira approves access requests submitted by Leon. Leon cannot approve requests from Mira.

variants.text: Leon approves access requests from Mira for the Cedar workspace.

expected.rationale: Reverses the approver and requester while preserving both names.

sources.text: For the Cedar workspace, Leon approves access requests submitted by Mira.

variants.text: Leon approves access requests from Mira for the Cedar workspace.

expected.rationale: The identical candidate is supported under this different governing context.

families.capability: Preserve which object a variable describes
families.reader_task: A reader checks the configured upload limit for an image or an archive.

sources.text: The configured limit per image upload is {image_limit}. The configured limit per archive upload is {archive_limit}. These are separate limits for different upload types.

variants.text: The limit per image upload is {image_limit}; the limit per archive upload is {archive_limit}.

expected.rationale: Preserves the governing claim for this reader task.

sources.text: The configured limit per image upload is {image_limit}. The configured limit per archive upload is {archive_limit}. These are separate limits for different upload types.

variants.text: Image uploads have a limit of {image_limit}, and archive uploads have a limit of {archive_limit}.

expected.rationale: Changes wording while preserving the governing claim.

sources.text: The configured limit per image upload is {image_limit}. The configured limit per archive upload is {archive_limit}. These are separate limits for different upload types.

variants.text: The limit per image upload is {archive_limit}; the limit per archive upload is {image_limit}.

expected.rationale: Swaps the image and archive upload limits even though both placeholders are preserved.

sources.text: In this fixture, the configured limit per image upload is {archive_limit}, and the configured limit per archive upload is {image_limit}. The variable names are legacy identifiers; these bindings are authoritative.

variants.text: The limit per image upload is {archive_limit}; the limit per archive upload is {image_limit}.

expected.rationale: The identical candidate is supported under this different governing context.
